💵 "The Nasdaq just added $1 trillion!" You've probably seen it today. Here's what it really means.

📈 What happened: US shares rallied strongly on Monday. At the time of writing, the tech-heavy Nasdaq was up about 3%, the S&P 500 more than 2%, and the Dow over 1,000 points. Chip companies led the rebound after last week's sell-off in AI stocks. Nvidia went the other way and fell.

🤔 The "$1 trillion": that's how much the total value of the companies' shares went up during the day (some reports say $1.5 trillion for all US shares). It is NOT $1 trillion of new cash flowing into the market. If share prices fall tomorrow, that value shrinks just as quickly. It's paper value until the close, and even then it can change the next day.

🇿🇦 What it means for you: many South African retirement annuities, unit trusts and tax-free savings accounts hold global shares, including big US tech companies. A day like this lifts their value; a bad week pulls it down. What counts for your savings is the long run, not one exciting day.

Education, not financial advice.
